experiments.name: Cold test of the SPARC REBCO toroidal-field model coil at 20 K with 20 bar supercritical helium and 40.5 kA terminal current (20.1 T self-field)
experiments.plain_name: Power a 10-tonne high-temperature-superconductor fusion magnet to 20 tesla while cooling it with 20 K helium gas
experiments.description: Representative-scale test of the no-insulation REBCO SPARC Toroidal Field Model Coil at the MIT PSFC test facility: the 10,058 kg coil sits in a 20 m3 vacuum cryostat with LN2 radiation shields, is cooled by 20 K supercritical helium (10-20 bar) from a cryocooler-based 600 W circulation system and is energised through 50 kA LN2-cooled REBCO current leads to 40.5 kA, producing 20.1 T peak field on conductor (the field is generated by the coil itself, so no external magnet is required).

requirements.rationale: The coil is operated with 20 K supercritical helium; the cryostat/cooling plant must hold the test article at 20 K.
requirements.document_title: The SPARC Toroidal Field Model Coil Program (Hartwig et al., arXiv:2308.12301, IEEE Trans. Appl. Supercond. 2024)
requirements.quote: A novel liquid-free cryocooler-based cryogenic system provided 20 K supercritical helium.

requirements.rationale: Full-performance test required 40.5 kA of terminal current delivered through the facility current leads.

experiments.plain_name: Freeze deuterium fuel into ice bullets near 7 K and fire them at kilometres per second
experiments.description: High-speed pellet fuelling R&D for DEMO on the ENEA-ORNL four-barrel Ignitor Pellet Injector: D2 ice is frozen in situ in the barrels under constant gas pressure, then cooled to ~7 K and held stable before launch with two-stage pneumatic guns (barrels 1.9-4.4 mm). With a PT810 cooler the freezing zone only reached ~10 K and pellets broke above 2 km/s; a PT415 (1.5 W at 4.2 K) lowered it to ~7.5 K.

requirements.rationale: Pellet ice must be lowered to ~7 K and kept stable for the D2 projectiles to survive >3 km/s acceleration.

requirements.quote: temperatures need to be carefully controlled during pellet formation under a constant D2 gas pressure, and then smoothly lowered to ~7 K and kept stable to ensure good resistance of cryogenic projectiles.

requirements.rationale: The upgraded cooler chosen to improve ice quality provides 1.5 W at 4.2 K; the earlier 14 W at 20 K cooler gave only ~10 K and broken pellets.

experiments.name: In situ transient grating spectroscopy of thermal diffusivity and SAW speed of Cu-110 during 12.4 MeV Cu6+ ion irradiation at 30 K (variable 30-300 K, high vacuum)
experiments.plain_name: Shine lasers on a copper magnet material while an ion beam damages it at 30 K to see how its heat conduction degrades
experiments.description: MIT facility for fusion magnet materials: a 13 x 15 x 2 mm sample on a copper thermal strap cooled by a CVi CGR409 cryocooler sits in a vacuum chamber (~1e-4 Pa) on the CLASS 1.7 MV Tandetron beamline; laser TGS pump/probe beams and the ion beam overlap on the sample to monitor thermal diffusivity and surface acoustic waves during irradiation at 30 K (apparatus range 30-300 K).

requirements.rationale: The irradiation and in situ TGS were performed at 30 K.

requirements.quote: An irradiation is then performed at 30 K, showcasing the thermal diffusivity and sound speed evolution of Cu-110 under self-ion irradiation.
